topics.name: used to / would for past habits

options: When does the school picnic start?
When do the school picnic start?
When the school picnic does start?
questions.rule: In a wh- question, put does before a singular subject: When does the picnic start?

options: The sheep stood beneath of the trees.
The sheep stood beneath to the trees.
The sheep stood beneath the trees.
questions.rule: Beneath is a preposition by itself. Don't add of or to after it.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: For a past habit, say used to + base verb: he used to walk.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After does, use the base verb: Why does Aryan stare...?

questions.after: clear that we could see the pebbles.
questions.rule: so + adjective + that shows a result: so clear that we could see.
Things are hidden in the grass, inside it.
Wh- word + do + subject + verb: Where do the cows stand?

chat: What did you use to do on Sundays when you were in Class 3?
options: I used to fly kites with my cousins.
I use to flying kites with my cousins.
I used to flew kites with my cousins.
questions.rule: used to is always followed by the base verb: used to fly.

questions.source: The boy is too tired to walk.
options: The boy is so tired that he cannot walk.
The boy is so tired that he can walk.
The boy is very tired that he cannot walk.
questions.rule: too ... to becomes so ... that + a negative: so tired that he cannot walk.

questions.prompt: Frame a question to get the answer 'from the terrace'.
questions.source: Kabir watches the sunset from the terrace.
options: Where does Kabir watches the sunset from?
Where does Kabir watch the sunset from?
Where Kabir does watch the sunset from?
questions.rule: After does, use the base verb: Where does Kabir watch...?

options: The music was too loud for us to heard the birds.
The music was too loud for us to hear the birds.
The music was too loud that we hear the birds.
questions.rule: too + adjective + for someone + to + base verb: too loud for us to hear.

options: We would to sit by the lake every evening.
Did you used to read comics as a child?
We used to sit by the lake every evening.
questions.rule: Say used to sit or would sit (no 'to' after would). In questions: Did you use to...?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Stars, the sun and the moon are in the sky.

questions.after: you ever watched a sky full of stars?
questions.rule: ever + past participle (watched) needs the present perfect: Have you ever watched...?

questions.before: When my father was young, he
questions.after: to cycle ten kilometres to school.
questions.rule: A past habit in a statement takes used to: he used to cycle.
too + adjective + to + verb: too deep to cross.

chat: Guess what! A bird has built a nest on our balcony.
options: Wow! What kind of bird it is?
Wow! What kind of bird is it?
Wow! What kind of bird are it?
questions.rule: In a direct question the verb comes before the subject: What kind of bird is it?

chat: Where did you leave my cricket bat?
options: I left it behind of the door.
I left it behind the door.
I left it behind to the door.
questions.rule: behind needs no extra word after it: behind the door.

questions.source: As a child, Meena played in the rain every monsoon.
options: As a child, Meena used to played in the rain every monsoon.
As a child, Meena was used to play in the rain every monsoon.
As a child, Meena used to play in the rain every monsoon.
questions.rule: Past habit: used to + base verb (play). 'was used to' means 'was familiar with'.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: used to + base verb (go). The story is in the past, so: they ate from their hands.

options: Who were you talking to on the phone?
Who you were talking to on the phone?
Who was you talking to on the phone?
questions.rule: Helping verb before the subject, and were goes with you: Who were you talking to?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Use so ... that with a full clause after it: so narrow that we could not ride.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After did, use the base form: Did she use to tell...?

questions.before: We sat on the bench and watched the boats sail
questions.rule: across = from one side to the other. between/among need two or more things.
Wh- word + does + subject + base verb: How does your family relax?

chat: Shall we go to the hill to watch the sunrise tomorrow?
options: I'd love to, but the hill is too far for us to walking.
I'd love to, but the hill is so far for us to walk.
I'd love to, but the hill is too far for us to walk.
questions.rule: too + adjective + for us to + base verb. so needs that + a clause.

chat: Do you still play the guitar, Sana?
options: No, I use to play it, but now I don't have time.
No, I used to play it, but now I don't have time.
No, I used to playing it, but now I don't have time.
questions.rule: A habit that has stopped: I used to play (used + to + base verb).

questions.source: The poet wants us to enjoy nature.
options: Does the poet wants us to enjoy nature?
Does the poet want us to enjoy nature?
Do the poet want us to enjoy nature?
questions.rule: Does + singular subject + base verb: Does the poet want...?

questions.source: The mangoes are so high that Riya cannot reach them.
options: The mangoes are too high that Riya cannot reach.
The mangoes are too high to Riya reach.
The mangoes are too high for Riya to reach.
questions.rule: too + adjective + for someone + to + verb, and drop the negative: too high for Riya to reach.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: He walks every evening (habit, singular). We listen to something.

options: When I was little, I used to collecting shells on the beach.
When I am little, I used to collect shells on the beach.
When I was little, I used to collect shells on the beach.
questions.rule: Past time needs was, and used to takes the base verb: used to collect.

options: How long have you been waiting under this tree?
How long you have been waiting under this tree?
How long have you been wait under this tree?
questions.rule: Present perfect continuous question: How long have you been waiting?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With a length of time, use for: has lived here for ten years.

questions.after: difficult that nobody in the class could answer it.
questions.rule: so + adjective + that. 'such' needs a noun (such a hard question).

questions.after: you been learning the sitar, Anaya?
questions.rule: been learning needs have with you: How long have you been learning?

questions.prompt: Make a sentence about the past.
questions.rule: There used to be = something existed in the past but not now.

options: I was sit under the neem tree, reading a book.
I was sitting under the neem tree, reading a book.
I was sitting under of the neem tree, reading a book.
questions.rule: Past continuous: was sitting. under needs no extra 'of'.

questions.source: Nikhil was too busy to notice the rainbow.
options: Nikhil was so busy that he cannot notice the rainbow.
Nikhil was so busy that he could notice the rainbow.
Nikhil was so busy that he could not notice the rainbow.
questions.rule: too ... to becomes so ... that + negative, in the same tense: so busy that he could not notice.

questions.source: Meera asked me, "Where do you go on Sundays?"
options: Meera asked me where did I go on Sundays.
Meera asked me where I went on Sundays.
Meera asked me where you went on Sundays.
questions.rule: Reported question: statement word order, you becomes I, and go becomes went.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: used to live; beside = next to (besides = also); past story, so he never felt tired.

options: The poem was such moving that many of us had tears in our eyes.
The poem was so moving that many of us had tears in our eyes.
The poem was too moving that many of us had tears in our eyes.
questions.rule: Adjective alone: so moving that. 'such' needs a noun; 'too' does not pair with 'that'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After did, always use the base verb: did you see?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: We rest in the shade, inside the shaded area.

questions.before: Nowadays Grandma is busy with her phone, but she
questions.after: spend hours watching the birds in the garden.
questions.rule: Old habit, now stopped: she used to spend. 'is used to' would need 'spending'.
so + adjective + that + result clause: so still that it looked like glass.

chat: My cousin is coming from Canada next week.
options: That's great! How long is she going to stay?
That's great! How long she is going to stay?
That's great! How long is she go to stay?
questions.rule: Question order: wh- word + is + subject + going to + base verb.

chat: Why didn't you finish the race, Arjun?
options: The sun was too hot that I felt dizzy halfway through.
The sun was so hot that I feel dizzy halfway through.
The sun was so hot that I felt dizzy halfway through.
questions.rule: so ... that + result, and keep the past tense: so hot that I felt dizzy.

questions.prompt: Rewrite using 'would' for the past habit.
questions.source: Every evening, Grandpa used to tell us stories under the stars.
options: Every evening, Grandpa would told us stories under the stars.
Every evening, Grandpa would to tell us stories under the stars.
Every evening, Grandpa would tell us stories under the stars.
questions.rule: would + base verb also shows a repeated past action: Grandpa would tell us stories.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: After do/did use the base verb (notice, stop). We rush and check.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Past story: we ate. We walk across fields and climb up a hill.
